Plot the trend of genes over the samples

Source: R/plot_trend.R
plot_trend.Rd

Plots, for the given genes, the mean normalized count of their barcodes in each sample (taken from the data table), with a regression line. It shows whether a hit decreases (or increases) over time in the selected samples.

Usage

plot_trend(
  screenR_Object,
  genes,
  group_var,
  alpha = 0.5,
  se = FALSE,
  point_size = 1,
  line_size = 1,
  nrow = 1,
  ncol = 1,
  scales = "free"
)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object.

genes

The names of the genes to plot.

group_var

The values of the Treatment column of the data table (see get_sample_table) of the samples to plot, for example the early time points and the treated samples.

alpha

The opacity of the confidence band, between 0 and 1. Default 0.5.

se

Whether to draw the confidence band of the regression line. Default FALSE.

point_size

The size of the points. Default 1.

line_size

The width of the regression line. Default 1.

nrow

The number of rows of panels, when several genes are plotted.

ncol

The number of columns of panels, when several genes are plotted.

scales

The scales of the panels: "free" (default), "fixed", "free_x" or "free_y".

Value

A ggplot object.

See also

compute_slope, filter_by_slope, plot_boxplot

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))

plot_trend(object, genes = "Gene_42", group_var = c("T1", "T2", "TRT"))


plot_trend(object,
    genes = c("Gene_42", "Gene_100"),
    group_var = c("T1", "T2", "TRT"),
    nrow = 2
)
